title: Research Analyst: sources, claims and visual facts

criteria.check: Every number, date, quotation and causal claim in the script appears in research/sources.md with publisher, title, year and URL.
criteria.why: Numbers on screen come only from sources.

criteria.check: Primary or official sources (statistics agencies, filings, peer-reviewed papers, archives, major newspapers) back the key claims; blogs and aggregators are not the only source of a claim.
Spot-checked claims match their sources: the figure, its unit, its year and what it measures.
criteria.why: A misread unit or year is the commonest error.

criteria.check: Every scene stating a number, date, quotation or causal claim has verify: true and a verify_note naming its source.
criteria.why: The human reviewer checks those scenes.

criteria.check: Where sources disagree, the script says so or uses the conservative figure, and a warning names the disagreement.
research/visual_facts.json covers every recurring person, vehicle, machine, building and place on screen, each with a specific name, visible features and a source.
criteria.why: Generic prompts make the model draw modern or wrong things.

criteria.check: Nothing in the frame prompts or visual facts is out of period or out of place for the era (vehicles, uniforms, technology, buildings, flags).
criteria.why: Anachronisms are what viewers notice and comment on.

criteria.check: For recent or ongoing topics, the newest figures are used and their date is stated.
criteria.why: Stale numbers date the video at once.
